articles.title: Watch: Three times Trump has promised money to Americans
articles.summary: The BBC's Samira Hussain looks at the president's past claims after he announced he would pay American adults $5,000 if Republicans win in the midterm elections.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump says he would give $5,000 to every American adult if the midterm elections go his way. Turning that promise into reality, however, would face significant hurdles. articles.standfirst: Candidato da Unidade Popular ao governo de Santa Catarina fez campanha na cidade mais populosa do estado nesta quinta-feira (10).
articles.summary: Candidato da Unidade Popular ao governo de Santa Catarina fez campanha na cidade mais populosa do estado nesta quinta-feira (10).
articles.body:
Laís Chaud conversa com movimento de mulheres e panfleta em Joinville nesta quinta (10) — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

A candidata ao governo de Santa Catarina Laís Chaud (UP) cumpriu agenda de campanha nesta quinta-feira (10) em Joinville, cidade mais populosa do estado.

Laís almoçou com mulheres do movimento Olga Benário e no começo da tarde, distribuiu panfletos em frente a uma indústria. À noite, participa de uma reunião com famílias da região.

Questionada pela NSC TV , Laís Chaud respondeu como pretende atuar junto ao governo federal para garantir recursos para Santa Catarina.

"Começar aplicando o dinheiro que hoje o Jorginho recebe e não usa, como no combate à violência contra as mulheres, fazendo grandes investimentos em espaços que acolham as mulheres vítimas de violência, segundo com a presidente Samara Martins, 80, fazer a auditoria da dívida pública, acabar com o bolsa banqueiro e garantindo, assim, maiores investimentos federais para o Estado".

🔍 A campanha eleitoral de 2026 iniciou no dia 16 de agosto em todo o país. Desde esta data, candidatos estão autorizados a pedir votos e realizar comícios, caminhadas, debates e divulgar suas propostas em rádio, TV e internet, seguindo as regras estabelecidas pela Justiça Eleitoral.

O primeiro turno das eleições de 2026 será realizado em 4 de outubro. O segundo turno, se for necessário, está marcado para 25 de outubro. Em Santa Catarina , os partidos definiram oito nomes na disputa pelo governo. São eles:

articles.summary: Shows, espetáculos teatrais, cinema, passeios e exposições movimentam a capital paraense e a região metropolitana neste fim de semana.
articles.body:
Atrações da agenda cultural do g1 Pará no fim de semana. — Foto: Reprodução

Uma agenda diversificada com apresentações musicais, teatro, programação nos cinemas, passeios literários e exposições gratuitas movimenta a cidade de Belém e a região nos próximos dias.

Entre os destaques estão a apresentação do cantor Alexandre Pires com o projeto "Pagonejo Bão" ; o Me Leva Festival trazendo Belo e grandes nomes do pagode nacional ; além da comédia dramática "O Começo do Fim" , protagonizada por Isabel Fillardis e Well Aguiar no Theatro da Paz.

A programação também conta com shows de rock, música eletrônica, festas de brega, batalhas de rima e experiências imersivas para fãs de séries coreanas.

Espetáculo 'O Começo do Fim' — Foto: Divulgação

Protagonizada por Isabel Fillardis e Well Aguiar, a comédia dramática propõe uma reflexão sobre os desafios das relações afetivas e a reconstrução da vida após a separação. Com humor e sensibilidade, a peça aborda temas como guarda compartilhada, saúde mental e racismo estrutural, destacando-se também por ser um espetáculo sustentável com elementos de ancestralidade amazônica.

📅 Quando: Sexta-feira (11) e sábado (12), às 20h; domingo (13), às 19h

💲 Quanto: Ingressos à venda pela plataforma Sympla e na bilheteria do Theatro da Paz

➡ Mais informações: No site ou na bilheteria do local

Alexandre Pires – Pagonejo Bão — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram @leolimaphotographer

O cantor traz a Belém o projeto "Pagonejo Bão", com um repertório que reúne os maiores sucessos de sua carreira. A apresentação promete uma estrutura premium e é voltada para o público adulto.

📅 Quando: Sábado (12), a partir das 23h30

📍 Onde: Hangar - Centro de Convenções — Av. Doutor Freitas, s/n, Marco, Belém

💲 Quanto: Não informado no material de divulgação

➡ Mais informações: Ingressos à venda pelo site Bilheteria Digital e nos pontos físicos Sonho dos Pés, Café da Agosto e Kings Sneakers

Dodô do Grupo Pixote — Foto: Rony Aires/Prefeitura de Santarém

📅 Quando: Domingo (13), com abertura dos portões às 16h

📍 Onde: Estacionamento do Mangueirão, Belém

💲 Quanto: Ingressos à venda pelo site Q2 Ingressos e nos pontos físicos Peça Rara (Gentil Bittencourt e Duque de Caxias) e lojas Hering (Pátio Belém, Boulevard e Parque Shopping)

O repertório transita entre a música sacra e clássicos da música popular brasileira e latino-americana, com participações especiais da soprano Thaina Souza e da mezzo-soprano Laura Gentile.

O show conta com a participação do grupo Molho Negro, que retorna à cidade onde surgiu para dividir o palco e celebrar a parceria entre as bandas.

Na montagem, os atores Álvaro Assad e Marcio Moura assumem a atuação e a manipulação dos personagens utilizando mímica, humor, música e objetos do cotidiano (como ralos e vassouras) que se transformam em cena, estimulando a imaginação de crianças e adultos.

articles.title: TH Jóias vira réu por tráfico e corrupção em esquema na Alerj | G1
articles.standfirst: Em decisão unânime, TRF2 recebe denúncia contra organização atuante na Alerj e governo estadual. Além de TH, viraram réus mais 5 pesssoas, entre elas 2 ex-secretários estatuais do governo do RJ.
articles.summary: TH Jóias e outros cinco acusados, incluindo ex-secretários estaduais, responderão por tráfico e corrupção em esquema investigado na Operação Zargun.
articles.body:
Índio do Lixão e TH Joias — Foto: Reprodução

A Justiça Federal tornou réus o ex-deputado estadual TH Joias (Thiego Raimundo de Oliveira Santos), do MDB-RJ, e outros cinco acusados de envolvimento em um esquema de corrupção, tráfico de drogas e contrabando ligado ao Comando Vermelho, investigado na Operação Zargun.

A denúncia do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) foi aceita pela 1ª Seção do Tribunal Regional Federal da 2ª Região (TRF2) nesta quinta-feira (10) por unanimidade (seis votos)

Além do ex-parlamentar, tornaram-se réus Gabriel Dias de Oliveira (Índio), Luiz Eduardo Cunha Gonçalves (Dudu), o ex-secretário estadual Alessandro Pitombeira Carracena (Esportes) e o delegado de Polícia Federal Gustavo Stteel ( veja abaixo os crimes atribuídos a cada um deles ).

Na denúncia, o MPF apontou a estabilidade de uma organização ligada à facção Comando Vermelho que infiltrou integrantes na Assembleia Legislativa do Rio de Janeiro (Alerj) e em secretarias estaduais para atuar no comércio ilegal de armas trazidas a comunidades do Rio de Janeiro a partir do Paraguai.

Os crimes atribuídos incluem ainda tráfico de drogas, contrabando de equipamentos antidrone e corrupção de agentes públicos.

O grupo importou clandestinamente bloqueadores de sinal de drone, de uso proibido para pessoas físicas e empresas, para sabotar e evitar o monitoramento das forças de segurança durante operações policiais.

Relembre reportagem com denúncias contra TH Joias:

De acordo com o MPF, o esquema envolvia a ocupação de cargos públicos, o vazamento de dados policiais e a facilitação de vantagens ilícitas.

Denunciados e crimes atribuídos pelo MP:

Thiego Raimundo de Oliveira Santos (“TH Joias”): organização criminosa majorada; tráfico de drogas (3x); contrabando de equipamentos (11x); corrupção ativa (13x); comércio ilegal de arma de fogo e munições

Gabriel Dias de Oliveira (“Índio”): organização criminosa majorada; tráfico internacional de armas de fogo (4x); comércio ilegal de arma de fogo e munições (6x); posse ou porte ilegal de arma de fogo de uso restrito (2); disparo de arma de fogo; tráfico de drogas (4x); contrabando de equipamentos (11x); corrupção ativa (13x)

Luiz Eduardo Cunha Gonçalves (“Dudu”): Organização criminosa majorada; tráfico internacional de armas de fogo; comércio ilegal de arma de fogo e munições (6x); posse ou porte ilegal de arma de fogo de uso restrito; tráfico de drogas (4); contrabando de equipamentos (11x); corrupção ativa (13x).

Alessandro Pitombeira Carracena : organização criminosa majorada; corrupção passiva (7x)

Gustavo Stteel: organização criminosa majorada; corrupção passiva (6x)

O g1 tenta contato com a defesa dos acusados.

Esta não é a única ação penal envolvendo TH Joias relacionada à Operação Zargun. Em agosto, a Primeira Turma do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) decidiu, por unanimidade, tornar réus TH, o ex-presidente da Alerj Rodrigo Bacellar, o desembargador federal Macário Ramos Júdice Neto, Jéssica de Oliveira Santos, esposa de TH, e Thárcio Nascimento Salgado.

Nesse processo, os acusados respondem por obstrução de investigação. Segundo a denúncia da Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), o grupo teria atuado entre os dias 2 e 3 de setembro de 2025 para vazar informações sobre a Operação Zargun, permitindo que TH, então deputado estadual e um dos principais alvos da ação, retirasse objetos de sua residência antes da chegada dos policiais.

A PGR afirma que os acusados agiram em conjunto para repassar informações sigilosas sobre a operação e, assim, dificultar a investigação de uma organização criminosa envolvida com tráfico internacional de armas e drogas, corrupção de agentes públicos e lavagem de dinheiro.

articles.title: Will foreign workers leave South Africa?
articles.summary: Anti-immigrant protests in the country are back.
articles.body:
Angry protesters in South Africa have taken to the streets again.

They have been demonstrating for months against undocumented foreigners living and working in the country.

Thousands of foreign workers have left South Africa in the last few months, after they were given a deadline by anti-immigrant groups. Now another deadline has been set for September 30.

Demonstrators are also calling on the government to take tougher action against undocumented immigrants.

As many of the protests have turned violent, how will the government in South Africa deal the issue of undocumented migrants?

articles.title: Tuberculose entre indígenas Kayapó: MPF pede ação urgente no Pará | G1
articles.standfirst: Dez casos foram registrados entre indígenas Kayapó de janeiro a agosto deste ano. Ação de prevenção e controle está prevista para começar na próxima segunda-feira (14).
articles.summary: Tuberculose entre indígenas Kayapó motiva ação do MPF em nove municípios do Pará para garantir tratamento e prevenção a partir desta segunda-feira.
articles.body:
O Ministério Público Federal (MPF) acionou a Justiça para incluir nove municípios do Pará em uma ação urgente de prevenção e controle da tuberculose entre indígenas Kayapó. A medida ocorre após registros da doença em comunidades indígenas no sul do estado. Segundo o Ministério da Saúde, dez casos foram confirmados de janeiro a agosto de 2026.

Os municípios são Cumaru do Norte, Redenção, Santana do Araguaia, Pau D'Arco, Bannach, Ourilândia do Norte, São Félix do Xingu, Tucumã e Altamira. As cidades ficam no entorno ou próximas à Terra Indígena Kayapó.

Uma ação de prevenção e controle da tuberculose está prevista para começar na próxima segunda-feira (14) nas aldeias vinculadas ao Polo Base de Tucumã. Segundo o Ministério da Saúde, o trabalho deve seguir até 18 de setembro.

Os dez casos registrados neste ano representam menos de um quarto dos 47 contabilizados em 2025, quando houve redução de 34% em relação ao ano anterior. Em 2024, foram registrados 80 casos entre indígenas Kayapó.

Uma morte também está sendo investigada, mas ainda não há confirmação de que a tuberculose tenha sido a causa ou contribuído para o óbito.

Um dos casos confirmados neste ano foi registrado em abril, em Santana do Araguaia, no sul do Pará. O paciente deveria retornar mensalmente a Belém para tratamento e acompanhamento.

Segundo documento do Distrito Sanitário Especial Indígena (DSEI) Kayapó do Pará, o indígena vinha se recusando a viajar para a capital por não ter recursos para se manter durante o deslocamento, principalmente para alimentação.

A situação levou o DSEI a solicitar uma reunião para discutir a ausência do paciente no acompanhamento do tratamento.

Em julho, outro caso foi confirmado em Cumaru do Norte. O paciente é um jovem de 18 anos.

Em 10 de agosto, a prefeitura do município notificou o DSEI sobre seis indígenas investigados por suspeita de tuberculose. Dois casos foram posteriormente descartados.

Cumaru do Norte fica a cerca de 200 quilômetros de Tucumã. Os dois municípios estão na região da Terra Indígena Kayapó.

Uma ação de prevenção, vigilância e controle da tuberculose prevista para ocorrer no Polo Base de Tucumã havia sido suspensa pelo Ministério da Saúde em 6 de agosto.

Segundo comunicado do órgão, a suspensão ocorreu após um incêndio atingir o centro de abastecimento da empresa responsável pela distribuição de medicamentos, imunobiológicos e insumos estratégicos para o Pará.

O incêndio afetou a disponibilidade de materiais necessários à ação e de insumos utilizados no diagnóstico e acompanhamento dos casos de tuberculose.

A nova ação está prevista para ocorrer entre os dias 14 e 18 de setembro nas aldeias atendidas pelo Polo Base de Tucumã.

Segundo o Ministério da Saúde, as medidas de enfrentamento à tuberculose entre os Kayapó incluem busca ativa de pessoas com sintomas respiratórios, investigação de contatos, diagnóstico e tratamento.

Em 2025, mais de 385 indígenas foram avaliados durante ações de busca ativa e investigação de contatos.

Em Ourilândia do Norte, o DSEI Kayapó também realiza uma ação ampliada para identificar possíveis casos e investigar pessoas que tiveram contato com pacientes. O trabalho inclui avaliação clínica, aplicação de prova tuberculínica (PPD), investigação de infecção latente, exames complementares e radiografia de tórax, quando indicada.

articles.standfirst: Cantora celebra retorno ao estado após 16 anos. Espetáculo vai encerrar a 20ª edição da festa neste domingo (13). Concentração será no Skate Park, na capital, a partir das 15h.
articles.summary: Cantora celebra retorno ao estado após 16 anos. Espetáculo vai encerrar a 20ª edição da festa neste domingo (13). Concentração será no Skate Park, na capital, a partir das 15h.
articles.body:
🏳️‍🌈 Com show marcado na 20ª Parada do Orgulho LGBTQIAPN+ do Acre , a propagadora do tecnobrega e porta-voz da cultura nortista Gaby Amarantos convocou os fãs a apresentação gratuita que ocorre neste domingo (13), no Centro de Rio Branco .

Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais da Associação de Gays, Lésbicas, Bissexuais, Travestis e Transexuais do Acre (Ahac), a estrela paraense celebrou o retorno ao estado acreano após 16 anos. "Alô Acre, estou tão feliz que vou chegar aí com meu rock doido para cantar na parada LGBTQIA+" , disse.

A edição deste ano tem como destaque as duas décadas da parada, que integra a agenda de celebração da diversidade e de promoção dos direitos humanos no estado. Somente no domingo (13), estão previstos cerca de 30 policiais militares e 110 profissionais de segurança privada.

Ainda conforme a artista, retornar ao estado acreano em um evento da diversidade é uma ocasião especial. "A mamãe vai chegar, meu amor, soltando todo o fogo. Eu quero todas com muito leque, vem", chamou a artista.

Gaby Amarantos faz show no encerramento da 20ª Parada do Orgulho LGBTQIAPN+ do Acre neste domingo (13) — Foto: Divulgação

A artista paraense esteve em Rio Branco em dezembro de 2010 para se apresentar no Festival Varadouro. À época, Gaby estava em plena ascensão nacional com o hit Ex Mai Love , que foi tema da novela Cheias de Charme em 2012, e logo estourou nas rádios brasileiras.

🗓️ A grande festa marcada para este domingo (13) vai ter a concentração no Skate Park, no Centro da capital acreana, a partir das 15h, com saída prevista para às 17h em direção à região do Palácio Rio Branco. Gaby deve ficar no palco das 19h às 22h. (Veja mais abaixo a programação)

Artista paraense comemorou a volta ao Acre em vídeo — Foto: Reprodução/ Instagram

Além de Amarantos, neste ano o agito também vai comemorado pela DJ Clementaum, que teve o seu bordão registrado na música "Sequência Cunt", do também DJ Pedro Sampaio. O evento vai ter concentração no Skate Park e termina no Palácio no centro da capital acreana.

Nesta sexta (11) , quando começa a 1ª Feira da Diversidade, o esquema prevê 28 policiais militares, dois policiais civis e quatro bombeiros . Já no sábado (12) , estão previsto policiais civis, agentes do Detran e bombeiros para atuar na segunda e bem-estar do evento.

A organização também definiu restrições para a entrada do público. No dia da parada, não será permitida a entrada de bebidas em garrafas de vidro e nem de geleiras. Conforme a Secretaria de Estado de Justiça e Segurança Pública (Sejusp), nos últimos quatro anos não houve ocorrências.

Além do reforço da segurança, uma das mudanças para a 20ª edição é o percurso da Parada do Orgulho no estado . Nesta quinta-feira (10), foi anunciada a alteração do trajeto, após estudos feitos pela Sejusp em conjunto com o Detran.

A mudança, conforme a organização, busca melhorar a segurança, a mobilidade urbana e o acesso dos serviços de saúde durante o evento.

A concentração no domingo (13) começa às 15h , no Skate Park , no Parque da Maternidade, e a saída está prevista para às 17h;

A caminhada deve seguir pela Avenida Ceará , com o retorno feito após o Estádio José de Melo e continuar pelas avenidas Brasil e Getúlio Vargas até a região do Palácio Rio Branco, no Centro da capital;

Após a chegada, o público vai poder acompanhar o show de Gaby Amarantos , previsto para ocorrer das 19h às 22h.

Ao todo a Semana da Diversidade do Acre, que teve início na última sexta-feira (4) e segue até o próximo domingo (13) em Rio Branco, conta com uma programação de atividades voltadas à educação, empreendedorismo, juventude, esporte e cultura.

Evento deste domingo (13) inicia às 15h no Skate Park e terá segurança reforçada — Foto: Fabio Rodrigues-Pozzebom

Na última sexta, a programação contou com um seminário sobre educação, empregabilidade e diversidade. Já no sábado (5) e domingo (6) ocorreu a 4ª edição do Campeonato de Vôlei LGBTI+.

As atividades seguiram e na última terça-feira (8), houve a palestra da atriz e humorista Nany People. Na quarta (9) e nesta quinta (10), ocorre uma atividade voltada para letramento e qualificação para empreendedores LGBTQIAPN+, onde também haverá um seminário de juventude.

A partir de sexta (11), as atividades são abertas ao público com a abertura da 1ª Feira da Diversidade, juntamente com o Concurso das Realezas da Diversidade para eleger a Rainha Gay, Rainha Trans e Rei Homem Trans .

A última parada em Rio Branco ocorreu em dezembro de 2024 e reuniu cerca de 7 mil pessoas. Em setembro do ano passado, a capital também recebeu o 1º Circuito Acreano da Diversidade , com shows nacionais e locais, oficinas, atividades esportivas e ações de enfrentamento à LGBTfobia.

articles.title: VÍDEO: Moradora escuta estralos e casa desaba em Curitiba | G1
articles.standfirst: Ela dormia no local com os dois netos, de 4 e 7 anos. Após ouvir os barulhos, todos saíram da casa. Ninguém se feriu.
articles.summary: Ela dormia no local com os dois netos, de 4 e 7 anos. Após ouvir os barulhos, todos saíram da casa. Ninguém se feriu.
articles.body:
Uma casa desabou na manhã desta quinta-feira (10), no bairro Xaxim, em Curitiba .

Durante a madrugada, a aposentada Terezinha Aparecida da Cruz dormia em um dos cômodos junto com os dois netos, de 4 e 7 anos, quando acordou ouvindo barulhos da estrutura. Imediatamente ela saiu do local com as crianças.

A Defesa Civil foi acionada, isolou o local e, pouco tempo depois, a estrutura desabou.

"A casa começou a estralar, um estralo leve, eu acordei assustada. Quando eu vi, não deu tempo de mais nada porque já estava cedendo o assoalho para cima. Eu saí para fora de casa e vi o pilar aberto. Sai com as crianças para fora, com aquele medo de desabar tudo. Eu pensava que não ia cair, mas agora, olhando, acabou de cair. Dói o coração", lamentou, emocionada.

Apesar das perdas materiais, ninguém se feriu.

"Agradeço a Deus por ter tirado meus netos a tempo. Não sei o que seria de mim sem eles aqui. Agora, vida que segue. Preparar tudo de novo para reconquistar o que foi perdido", afirmou Terezinha.

Terezinha conseguiu sair a tempo da casa, que tempo depois, desabou — Foto: Reprodução

Casa desabou em Curitiba — Foto: Defesa Civil

Temporais causaram estragos em cidades do Paraná entre a noite de quarta-feira (9) e a madrugada desta quinta-feira (10). Houve queda de árvores, granizo, alagamentos e destelhamentos.

Em Curitiba, a Defesa Civil registrou 57,6 milímetros de chuva em 12 horas. O maior acumulado foi registrado no bairro Caximba. A maior rajada de vento chegou a 49 km/h.

Em Rio Branco do Sul e Almirante Tamandaré , na Região Metropolitana de Curitiba, também foram registrados alagamentos e quedas de muros.

Em Terra Roxa , no Oeste, a Defesa Civil registrou 55 milímetros de chuva em apenas 30 minutos. Pelo menos 15 árvores caíram durante o temporal. Também houve queda de granizo, alagamentos e destelhamentos de casas.

Em Foz do Iguaçu , também no Oeste, pelo menos seis árvores caíram durante a tempestade, algumas atingindo redes elétricas. Também houve registro de granizo e, segundo a Defesa Civil, não houve registro de pessoas desabrigadas, desalojadas ou feridas.

articles.body:
Jorginho Mello visitou obras e se reuniu com apoiadores no Vale do Itajaí nesta quinta (10) — Foto: NSC TV/Reprodução

O candidato à reeleição ao governo de Santa Catarina Jorginho Mello ( PL ) cumpriu agenda de campanha nesta quinta-feira (10) no Vale do Itajaí.

Pela manhã, visitou obras em Indaial. Depois, se encontrou com apoiadores e outros candidatos da coligação para almoço em uma sociedade recrativa, onde conversou com eleitores e discursou.

Pela tarde, seguiu para um encontro com apoiadores no município de Agronômica e à noiteestará na cidade em Rio do Sul, onde também deve se reunir com lideranças partidárias.

Questionado pela NSC TV , Jorginho Mello respondeu sobre como pretende atuar junto ao governo federal para garantir recursos para Santa Catarina.

"Primeiro, vou trabalhar muito para o Flávio ganhar a eleição. O governo que tá aí não gosta de Santa Catarina. E depois, independentemente disso, eu vou fazer Santa Catarina ser respeitada. Nós não vamos baixar a cabeça pra ninguém".

articles.title: Elmano quer ampliar descentralização das políticas de cultura no Ceará | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PT ao Governo do Estado cumpriu agenda de campanha em Fortaleza nesta quinta-feira (10) e comentou propostas para as áreas de cultura e esporte.
articles.summary: Candidato do PT ao Governo do Estado cumpriu agenda de campanha em Fortaleza nesta quinta-feira (10) e comentou propostas para as áreas de cultura e esporte.
articles.body:
Elmano de Freitas, candidato à reeleição ao cargo de governador do Estado — Foto: Fabiane de Paula/SVM

O governador e candidato à reeleição Elmano de Freitas ( PT ) defendeu, nesta quinta-feira (10), ampliar o processo de descentralização das políticas em cultura no Ceará para um eventual segundo mandato . O petista também destacou que pretende concluir equipamentos culturais em construção no estado, durante uma caminhada da campanha no bairro Álvaro Weyne, em Fortaleza.

"Nós queremos poder descentralizar cada vez mais, seja nos bairros da periferia das grandes cidades, como especialmente na nossa Região Metropolitana, mas também para o interior. Nós queremos construir pelo menos 20 equipamentos de cultura, vários deles já estão em construção e nós queremos concluir. [Vamos] colocar para funcionar os equipamentos culturais no interior e nos bairros das nossas cidades para poder, com isso, toda a população ter acesso aos bens culturais e programações gratuitas", disse Elmano.

Elmano afirmou ainda que quer aumentar os investimentos na Ceará Filmes, empresa pública estadual criada em dezembro de 2025 cujo objetivo é fomentar a indústria do audiovisual cearense.

O candidato à reeleição também defendeu a política de editais para a cultura, garantindo o incentivo do Estado aos pequenos produtores culturais.

"É muito importante nós mantermos editais, em que os grupos culturais das cidades e dos bairros possam acessar recurso público, garantindo, com isso, financiamento para fazer as atividades que são organizadas pela sociedade. Nem tudo deve ser feito apenas pelo governo, muita coisa boa é feita pelo povo e o povo apenas quer ter a condição de ter um edital, um recurso, para organizar essas atividades. A política mais adequada é o edital, porque ele é democrático, porque todo mundo pode disputar, porque todo mundo pode participar e é transparente", afirmou.

Sobre propostas para a área do esporte, Elmano também defendeu o uso de editais públicos para garantir a atuação de projetos como os que atendem jovens de comunidades pelo estado.

"Eu creio que, nas comunidades, o elemento mais importante é nós também termos editais, para que clubes, para que grupos de jovens, para que entidades que fazem trabalho com crianças e com jovens possam acessar recursos para ampliar os seus projetos. Hoje eu tenho um projeto que atende 50 crianças, 40 crianças, mas que pode passar a atender 100, 150. Isso é muito importante para capilarizar e chegar na ponta, para jovens e crianças praticarem mais esporte", afirmou o candidato.

Elmano destacou que pretende também ampliar a construção das areninhas nos municípios, mas não especificou quantas novas unidade pretende fazer em uma nova gestão. Segundo ele, já foram 500 construídas, sendo 150 delas entregues no seu governo. De acordo com o governador, há uma demanda também por quadras de beach tennis .

"Nós estamos aprendendo que muda, às vezes, tem um certo esporte que aparece e ganha a simpatia da população. Uma hora é beach tennis, outra hora é outro esporte. Portanto, é importante nós termos equipamentos que possam ter essa flexibilidade para se ajustar aquilo que cada pessoa quer fazer a cada momento".

articles.title: The 3 coolest new Apple devices coming out this fall
articles.summary: A folding iPhone, affordable noise cancellation and a watch that can turn back time: Three cool Apple gadgets for fall.
articles.body:
If you buy something through a link in this article, we may earn commission.

Apple wrapped its latest, and likely biggest, product launch event of 2026 yesterday. As we expected, the iPhone maker unveiled its first foldable phone, dubbed the iPhone Duo. Other companies have been making folding handsets for years, so why did it take Apple so long? From what we saw during the show, Apple took many lessons from its competitors — then added a few Apple flourishes — to create what looks like one seriously enviable (and seriously expensive) new device. The company also announced the latest series of Apple Watch that could help you go back in time, as well as new AirPods that block out the world. For those who need a catch-up, these are the three coolest Apple devices hitting shelves this fall.

1. The iPhone Duo: Multitasking and Duo FaceTime

No doubt Apple named its foldable phone "Duo" to strongly suggest it gives you two devices in one: A pocketable phone and a mini tablet. (That two-for-one mentality may also make it easier for some to stomach the $2,000 price tag.) If money were no issue, this is the phone I'd get.

The external screen measures 5.4-inches on the diagonal, which is about 90% the size of the 6.3-inch standard iPhone. Unfolded, you get a 7.6-inch display. Around back are two cameras, a 48MP fusion main lens and a 48MP fusion ultra wide lens that's the same as the iPhone 18 Pro. The phone is housed in a titanium chassis, uses the new A20 Pro chip and the smooth-opening hinge is made up of more than 100 components.

But enough about the hardware. The more interesting part is what the folding design allows the Duo to do. You can unfurl the phone halfway to create a tripod effect for the rear cameras. Set it on a table and not only will you be able to get a steady shot, but an AI-enabled Smart Take feature will take the picture automatically when everyone is in position.

The external screen lets you frame up selfies too, using the more powerful rear lenses to snap the shot. But arguably the most intriguing camera feature is Duo FaceTime, which lets the person you're talking to see both you and what you're looking at, and allows others in the room to participate in the call using the rear screen.

Apple redesigned the software and customized apps to automatically adapt the screen to how you're holding the phone, whether that's landscape, portrait, open or closed. With the Duo unfolded, you can take advantage of multitasking features that let you open two apps side-by-side. The Duo can even go into StandBy mode when it's not charging. Prop it on your night table like a tent for an alarm clock mode or stand it up like a book on your desk to see the dashboard and notifications.

The iPhone Duo will be open for pre-orders starting on October 16, with orders expected to ship October 23. The price starts at $1,999 for 256GB of storage and goes up to an eye-watering $3,199 for 2TB of storage.

2. AirPods 5: Noise cancellation for everyone

The AirPods 4 came out in 2024 and had a version with active noise cancellation (ANC) and a version without. Apple announced two versions of the AirPods 5 yesterday as well, but now both models have ANC. The more expensive version adds a longer battery life and a wirelessly recharging case.

Unlike AirPods Pro, standard AirPods have an "open-ear fit." That means they don't insert completely into your ear canal — as you might imagine, it's a little tougher to cancel out noise around you without that physical, ear-plug-like barrier. Apple says that thanks to new acoustic architecture and advanced computational audio, the AirPods 5 have 50% better noise reduction than their predecessors. That's good news for people who prefer not to stick things in their ear holes.

Both models also offer hands-free access to the new Siri AI which, from what we've seen , is far-and-away better than the old Siri. That means you'll be able to ask for contextualized, personalized info through your buds, such as, "What was that new restaurant Hannah texted me about?" then follow up Siri's answer with, "Give me walking directions."

The standard AirPods 5 will sell for $129 (the same price as the AirPods 4 without ANC). The AirPods 5 with the wireless charging case and bigger batteries will go for $149. You can pre-order both now and they'll be available starting September 18.

3. Apple Watch Series 12: Know your "health age" and revisit conversations

Is your smartwatch smart enough to help you turn back the clock? The newest Apple Watch is. OK, that's not technically true and, to be clear, Apple said nothing of the sort. But the new Apple Watch Series 12 does come equipped with new sensors and processors that feed into a Longevity tab in the redesigned Health App. Those metrics, along with uploaded lab results, can generate your "Health Age," which tells you how everything lines up with your actual age.

You can even take mobility and flexibility assessments using your watch and iPhone. Apple demoed a VO2-max test that tracks your movement with the phone's camera while heart rate and other measurements are picked up on your wrist.

As for going back in time and revisiting conversations, the Apple Watch combines an onboard microphone, new audio processors and AI models to enable a feature called Live Rewind. When someone says something and you didn't quite catch it, you can double press the digital crown and get a transcription on your watch of the last 15 seconds of audio the watch picked up.

Yes, that means, with this feature enabled, your watch is always listening — but to mitigate privacy concerns, the feature will play an audible chime and turn on a microphone indicator on your watch when Live Rewind is transcribing audio.

The Apple Watch Series 12 can also take notes during your conversations (much to the disappointment of AI note-taking device makers ). Siri Recap, when enabled, can create high-level summaries including key points of a conversation that you can find in the Siri app. For privacy's sake, the feature is designed to exclude taking down sensitive info like financial details, SSNs and ID numbers. Apple also said that the rewind and recap snippets are end-to-end encrypted and not accessible to Apple.

The Apple Watch Series 12 is available for pre-order now and starts at $399.

articles.title: 'Killer' bahu’s deadly game: Kanpur bizman sensed danger but ended up with 26 stab wounds and a slit throat
articles.summary: KANPUR: A murder planned to look like a heart attack allegedly turned into a brutal stabbing after 63-year-old businessman Vineet Minocha walked into .
articles.body: KANPUR: A murder planned to look like a heart attack allegedly turned into a brutal stabbing after 63-year-old businessman Vineet Minocha walked into his bedroom and noticed something unusual. The assailants allegedly panicked, attacked him with knives and fled, leaving Vineet with 26 stab wounds and a slit throat.According to investigators, Minocha's daughter-in-law Shalu Minocha, who police have accused of masterminding the murder, had allegedly instructed former employee Vishal Gautam and his acquaintance Raj Kishor to suffocate Vineet with a pillow so the death would appear natural.But the plan allegedly changed after Vineet walked into the bedroom around 11pm and noticed something unusual.Killers allegedly waited inside bedroomPolice said Shalu had approached Vishal, a former employee at Vineet's pharmaceutical store, and allegedly offered him Rs 6 lakh for the killing.She allegedly handed Vishal the original key to the family's apartment so that a duplicate could be made. Vishal then allegedly involved his unemployed acquaintance Raj Kishor, 30, promising him an advance of Rs 30,000.On September 5, Shalu allegedly told the two men that she, her husband Subrat and their son would be attending a party.Using the duplicate key, Vishal and Raj allegedly entered Ratan Orbit Apartment in Kalyanpur. Police said they initially faced resistance from the security guard but told him they were delivering medicines.Vishal allegedly registered himself under the fictitious name Shivam.After entering the apartment, the two men allegedly hid inside a bedroom and waited for Vineet to return.‘Heart attack’ plan goes awryInvestigators said the original plan was to suffocate Vineet with a pillow and make the killing look like a heart attack.The plan allegedly went awry when Vineet entered the bedroom at around 11pm and noticed something unusual.Police said he was stabbed repeatedly and his throat was slit before the accused fled. The postmortem found 26 stab wounds on Vineet's body.Police said the murder took place sometime between 10.30pm on Saturday and 3am on Sunday, while Vineet was alone in the four-room apartment.Shalu, husband were at lounge during murderWhile the alleged killing was taking place, Shalu and her husband were at Cosmozin Lounge in Tilak Nagar, police said.A video recorded by lounge staff showed Shalu dancing with Subrat to the Bollywood song “Tum To Dhokhebaaz Ho, Vaada Karke Bhool Jaate Ho”.Police said the footage confirmed their presence at the lounge that night.The lounge's CCTV DVR had no stored footage, but videos recorded by staff showed around 20-25 people, mostly couples, dancing to Bollywood songs. Shalu was seen wearing a dark purple gown while Subrat was dressed in a grey shirt.Police said Shalu's behaviour appeared normal and other guests at the lounge seemed unaware of what was allegedly unfolding at her home.Police allege Shalu stayed in touch with assailantsDespite being at the party, Shalu allegedly remained in contact with the two men through WhatsApp calls, messages and voice calls and allegedly guided them during the crime, according to investigators.Police arrested Shalu on Monday after Vishal allegedly told them that he had killed Vineet on her instructions in return for money.Police said Shalu allegedly admitted her involvement in the presence of female police personnel after being confronted with Vishal.CCTV dispute allegedly behind murderInvestigators suspect the alleged murder was linked to a dispute over CCTV cameras installed by Vineet inside the apartment around 15-20 days before his death.Police said Shalu objected to the cameras, claiming they violated her privacy and caused her emotional distress. No valuables stolen from apartmentInvestigators said CCTV footage showed Vishal and Raj leaving the apartment after the murder. The two were arrested following an encounter late Sunday.Police said nothing was stolen from the apartment, strengthening their suspicion that the killing was motivated by personal enmity rather than robbery.Section 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to criminal conspiracy, has also been added to the case.The investigation is continuing, with police examining the alleged communications between Shalu and the assailants and the circumstances surrounding Vineet's murder.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kanpur | Silver Rate in Kanpur | Bank Holidays in Kanpur | Public Holidays in Kanpur | Kanpur AQI | Weather in Kanpur | Petrol Price in Kanpur | Diesel Price in Kanpur | CNG Price in Kanpur | LPG Price in KanpurStay updated with the latest Kanpur news. articles.title: India may have produced enough plutonium for 140 to 225 nukes, might have assembled up to 190 warheads: US study
articles.summary: News News: New Delhi: At least 30 additional nuclear warheads for new missiles under production have been added to India’s 160 existing warheads for operational .
articles.body: New Delhi: At least 30 additional nuclear warheads for new missiles under production have been added to India’s 160 existing warheads for operational launchers, taking the total such warheads with the country to 190, according to a US nonprofit policy think tank.The article, titled 'India's Nuclear Weapons – 2026', published on Wednesday, said, “India continues to modernise its nuclear arsenal, with several new weapon systems fielded in recent years and several more under development to complement or replace existing nuclear-capable aircraft, land-based delivery systems, and sea-based systems. We estimate that India may have produced enough military plutonium for 140 to 225 nuclear warheads and might have assembled up to 190. With more weapon systems in development, the country’s warhead stockpile will likely increase further.”The nuclear notebook is researched and written by the staff of the Federation of American Scientists’ Nuclear Information Project director Hans M Kristensen, associate director Matt Korda, research and project manager Mackenzie Knight-Boyle, and senior research associate Eliana Johns. “We estimate that India currently operates nine different nuclear-capable systems: two aircraft, six land-based ballistic missiles, and one sea-based ballistic missile. At least two more systems are in development and nearing completion and are to be fielded with the armed forces within one or a few years,” the report said.As India does not publish numbers of its its nuclear weapon stockpile, analyses and estimates made in the research are derived from a combination of open sources: state-originating data like govt statements, declassified documents; non-state-originating data like media reports, think tank analyses, and industry publications; and commercial satellite imagery.India is one of only a handful of countries believed to be producing both highly enriched uranium (HEU) and weapons-grade plutonium and its HEU production is largely assumed to be focused on producing fuel for its growing number of nuclear-powered vessels and submarines, the report said.“India’s source of weapons-grade plutonium has been the aging 100-megawatt (MWt) Dhruva plutonium production reactor at Bhabha Atomic Research Centre complex near Mumbai, and until 2010 the CIRUS reactor at the same location. After more than a decade of delays, India’s new 500-MWt Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at the Indira Gandhi Center for Atomic Research near Kalpakkam reached first criticality in April 2026. Fuelled by a stockpile of reactor-grade plutonium separated from India’s first-generation power reactors, the new reactor irradiates a “blanket” of uranium or thorium to produce Plutonium-239 and Uranium-233. If operated at 80% efficiency, the PFBR could hypothetically produce an estimated 140 kg of plutonium-239 per year, sufficient for up to 35 nuclear warheads,” the article said elaborating on India’s nuclear programme.“Several more fast breeder reactors are planned, including two that are in pre-planning stage (FBR-1 and FBR-2) and will be located adjacent to the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor at Kalpakkam. If operated successfully, the breeder reactors could potentially increase significantly the amount of plutonium available for India’s nuclear warhead stockpile,” it further said.“As of the beginning of 2026, the International Panel on Fissile Materials estimated India to have produced approximately 730 kg (plus or minus about 170 kg) of weapon-grade plutonium,” the report said, adding, “Assuming 4 kg of plutonium per warhead, this would theoretically be sufficient for producing anywhere between 140 and 225 nuclear warheads.” However, this calculation comes with some caveats due to several uncertainties, the report indicated.“Regardless of the warhead designs, it is unlikely that India has used all its plutonium to produce warheads, and it may have kept some in reserve,” the report said, adding, “the size of India's nuclear stockpile also depends on the number and types of launchers that can deliver them, as it is unlikely that it would produce significantly more warheads than these systems can launch.”“India is committed to maintaining credible minimum deterrence and a posture of 'no first use' of nuclear weapons,” the Modi govt told Parliament recently. As compared to India’s estimated 170 nuclear warheads, Pakistan has an estimated stockpile of approximately 170 nuclear warheads, according to a recent SIPRI report.

articles.title: Stormont: Executive to meet again over budget offer
articles.summary: On Monday, Sir Chris Bryant visited Stormont and made an initial offer of £350m per year over the next three years to help stabilise the executive's finances.
articles.body:
The executive will hold further talks with the secretary of state on Friday to discuss the government's offer of money to resolve Stormont's budget deadlock.

On Monday, Sir Chris Bryant visited Stormont and made an initial offer of £350m per year over the next three years to help stabilise the executive's finances.

But executive parties said that did not go far enough and suggested that the government would need to increase its contribution in order for Stormont to balance its books this year.

It is understood the discussions on Friday morning will take place virtually.

The executive has repeatedly said it cannot agree a budget for this financial year without extra support from Westminster.

Following the passing of a deadline in August, Stormont officials were given legal powers to spend up to 95% of last year's funding in the absence of ministers agreeing the budget.

Multi-year budget plan 'will transform public services'

Treasury to give Stormont £400m in a bid to balance department budgets

Finance minister confident on multi-year budget

No formal deadline has been set in the talks with Westminster, but Number 10 is due to publish its budget on 28 October so there is an expectation from some Stormont sources that any financial settlement should be agreed before then.

Speaking after meeting the secretary of state on Monday , First Minister Michelle O'Neill said the executive was now in a "negotiation" with the government.

"We get to this juncture time after time, crisis point after crisis point - they need to fix the baseline.

"If they throw a few pounds on the table and walk away we'll end up back in this scenario."

DUP leader Gavin Robinson said the initial offer from the government "falls well short of even some of the pressures in one department, let alone across the Northern Ireland Executive".

"Anybody who says we just need to get on and agree this can explain the cuts that will come as a consequence," he added.

Could money be tied to reform of Stormont?

Alliance has said any agreement on a financial package should be tied to commitments to reform the Stormont institutions.

Its leader Naomi Long said it was important to have those conversations in parallel, ahead of the next assembly election in May 2027.

Ulster Unionist leader Jon Burrows said there was "going to have to be a meeting of minds between His Majesty's government and the political parties" on any financial arrangement.

"We certainly accept the premise that we need to come to this with credibility ....so we don't keep asking for more."

The SDLP - Stormont's official opposition - said the executive could not shirk its responsibility to agree a budget.

Its leader Claire Hanna also met the secretary of state on Monday to press the case for reforming the executive and assembly.

"We don't need months and months of negotiation in a stately home, everybody knows what needs to be done," she said.

"If they're not done we're going to be right back here and if we fail to put these mechanisms in place ahead of the next election we're facing into more lost years."

articles.title: Checks on e-commerce platforms from October: FSSAI
articles.summary: India News: New Delhi: Having secured nearly 2,000 convictions in food safety cases across the country, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is no.
articles.body: New Delhi: Having secured nearly 2,000 convictions in food safety cases across the country, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) is now stepping up enforcement, including holding e-commerce platforms responsible for products sold through them and proposing stricter action against high-fat, sugar and salt (HFSS) foods near schools, its CEO Rajit Punhani said Thursday.FSSAI will begin checks on e-commerce platforms from next month. Platforms will have to carry out due diligence and ensure that products listed on them comply with food safety regulations."We are holding e-commerce platforms responsible. They cannot take this plea that they are just aggregators, they are just platforms. It is your responsibility, your due diligence," Punhani said.FSSAI has already held consultations with e-commerce companies. Punhani identified e-commerce and labelling as two major consumer-focused reforms expected over the next year.The regulator has also proposed restricting the sale of HFSS food within 50 metres of schools to protect children from unhealthy food. Punhani said the earlier challenge was the absence of a clear definition of HFSS food. The Indian Council of Medical Research-National Institute of Nutrition, a govt nutrition research institute, has now provided criteria that FSSAI plans to use.On enforcement, Punhani said FSSAI had suspended licences, closed establishments and launched prosecutions. Around 600 people had been arrested in criminal cases involving unsafe food in the previous six months, he said. He cited around 1,900 convictions and 33,000 notices issued across India for food safety violations, including adulteration, mislabelling and substandard food.FSSAI is also tightening rules on food claims and marketing. It does not allow "100%" claims except in cases under litigation, while "pure" and "natural" can be used only for single-ingredient products, provided nothing has been added. The regulator has also written to Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade and the Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks over the use of "healthy" as a trademark.Punhani said the term "energy drink" would not be allowed on labels as it could mislead consumers, with such products classified as caffeinated beverages, while the proposed red warning system would also cover aerated, carbonated and caffeinated beverages. The regulator has issued notices to six celebrities over misleading food-related endorsements, with three having responded.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: SEN McCORMICK: The heroic passengers of Flight 93 showed America how to stand united
articles.summary: Todd Beamer's famous "Let's roll" rallied Flight 93 passengers to charge al Qaeda hijackers, and their six-minute fight changed the course of 9/11.
articles.body: Twenty-five years ago, 40 men and women showed uncommon courage on Flight 93. Today, we honor their sacrifice and their example on a field of honor forever in Shanksville, Pennsylvania. On the morning of 9/11, I was in a skyscraper in Pittsburgh as the attacks unfolded. We knew another plane had been hijacked somewhere over Pennsylvania, but we did not know where it was or where it was headed. Then came the news from Shanksville — and, later, the story of what its passengers and crew had done. Less than an hour after United Flight 93 left Newark, four al Qaeda terrorists seized the plane and forced the passengers and crew to the rear of the aircraft. Flight 93 was different from the other hijacked planes that morning because a ground delay gave its passengers time to learn of the attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon. When the plane turned toward Washington, they knew that Flight 93 had become another weapon of terror. 9/11 IS BECOMING HISTORY. MY GENERATION MUST MAKE SURE AMERICA NEVER FORGETS Through calls to loved ones and people on the ground, they learned what had happened in New York and at the Pentagon. They understood that the hijackers did not intend for them to survive and that countless more innocent lives were at stake. C.S. Lewis wrote that courage is "the form of every virtue at the testing point." For the ordinary Americans aboard Flight 93, that testing point came without warning — and within minutes they responded in an extraordinary, distinctly American way. They took a vote and made a plan. At 9:57 a.m., Todd Beamer, an account manager for Oracle, uttered the now-famous words, "Let’s roll," and they charged the cockpit and the knife-wielding jihadis. For six minutes, they fought to retake the plane. At 10:03, the plane flipped upside down and plowed into a farmer’s field near Shanksville. Their sacrifice denied the terrorists their target. Twenty-five years later, their example offers lessons not only about who we were then, but also who we must continue to be. 9/11 TAUGHT US DEADLY LESSONS. 25 YEARS LATER, WE NEED A NEW MODEL TO PREVENT ATTACKS We must remain vigilant in the face of evil. At home, that means rejecting the poisonous idea, voiced by Hasan Piker, that America "deserved 9/11." Abroad, it means taking seriously enemies who chant "Death to America" and mean it. We Americans do not go looking for a fight; but when called upon, we show the strength and courage that should make our enemies think twice. Even now, the men and women of the United States military are reminding the world that threats against America have consequences. Vigilance must be backed by strength. When the time to act arrives, the time to prepare has passed. The passengers and crew of Flight 93 had only minutes and whatever strength they could summon. Today, advances in AI, robotics and other technologies are transforming both the threats we face and the tools we have to defeat them. America needs the strongest military in the world, equipped with the best technology and ready to give those who serve every advantage when called to fight. Yet because evil is real, we must not blur the distinction between genuine evil and ordinary political disagreement. In those decisive minutes aboard Flight 93, no one asked who was a Republican or Democrat, where anyone came from or how anyone worshiped. They acted together as Americans. That same sense of common purpose swept the country after September 11 as strangers helped strangers, communities grieved together and a generation raised its hand to serve. Today, that unity can seem distant. Our politics too often turns disagreement into enmity and fellow Americans into adversaries. September 11 reminds us that before we are Republicans, Independents or Democrats, we are Americans. MIKE PENCE: THE NEXT GENERATION NEEDS FAITH IN GOD AND CONFIDENCE IN THE AMERICAN IDEAL From Gettysburg to Normandy to Shanksville, ordinary Americans have shown the spirit, courage and character that define America at its best. President George W. Bush said the terrorists discovered that "a random group of Americans is an exceptional group of people." The passengers and crew were students and retirees, an ironworker and an attorney, business travelers and flight attendants — ordinary people who answered an extraordinary call. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION But we cannot take that spirit for granted. Only 39% of Americans say they are "extremely proud" to be American, down from 70% in 2003, and pride is even lower among younger Americans. At the same time, too many boys and young men are struggling to find purpose and a path into adulthood. Character must be taught and cultivated. We must tell these stories, call the next generation to service, and teach them that courage means self-command, responsibility and putting others before themselves. NEW 9/11 MUSEUM EXHIBIT AIMS TO CONNECT YOUNGER AMERICANS TO THE ATTACKS THROUGH POWERFUL ARTIFACTS That is why I encourage every American to visit the Flight 93 National Memorial in Shanksville, where I will join others in remembrance today. Bring your children and grandchildren. Stand at the crash site and listen to the calls made in the flight’s final minutes — some to say goodbye, others to explain what was happening and what they intended to do about it. You cannot hear their voices and leave unchanged. Most of us will never face such an extraordinary test. But all of us are called, in ways large and small, to serve our country and leave it better for those who come after us. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP At their testing point, the heroes of Flight 93 showed us what America still requires of you, me and each of us: the clarity to recognize evil, the strength to confront it, the unity to stand together and the courage to put country before self.

articles.title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet
articles.summary: The government says the work will support thousands of jobs across the UK.
articles.body:
Work to create the UK's first battery-electric trains for long-distance main line services is set to begin in 2028, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.

The 29 new Adessia Stream trains are expected to enter service in 2034 and will be built at Alstom's Litchurch Lane factory in Derby.

The government said the investment of almost £1bn would help support more than 350 jobs at Alstom and a further 6,000 jobs across the UK supply chain.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the new trains would deliver "faster, more reliable journeys to the north and thousands of British jobs for the next generation".

He added: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came.

"And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities. Today, that starts to change."

The DfT said the trains would help deliver the Transpennine Route Upgrade's aim to boost capacity by 30%, with thousands of additional seats a day across the Pennines by the early to mid-2030s.

They will run between key destinations across the north including Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull.

The DfT added that journey times will be cut by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York.

The trains will be bought by Rock Rail and leased to TransPennine Express, the government added.

Alstom, which boasts the largest rolling stock train manufacturing site outside of China, secured a £370m contract in 2024 to produce 10 new London Elizabeth line trains.

This came less than three months after a redundancy consultation put 1,300 jobs at risk at its Litchurch Lane factory, which dates back to 1876.

Rob Whyte, managing director UK at Alstom, called the latest agreement a "landmark moment for Britain's railway".

He said: "We couldn't be prouder that the country's first main line battery-electric trains will be designed and built in Britain.

"The fleet will transform journeys across northern England while showcasing the very best of British engineering, innovation and advanced manufacturing."

In a statement, DfT said journeys on the new fleet would be "quieter, smoother and more reliable", while offering "improved accessibility, more luggage space and onboard Wi-Fi".

Step-free boarding - the "elimination of gaps between the train and platform" - are also being promised as part of a commitment to accessibility, alongside three dedicated wheelchair spaces, two accessible toilets, family-friendly areas and cycle and buggy storage on each train.

articles.title: ICE arrests Peruvian national accused of illegally voting in 2024 election as DHS cites similar cases
articles.summary: Mariana Alexandra Dewey, a Peruvian national, was arrested by ICE in Wichita after she allegedly voted illegally in the 2024 Kansas election.
articles.body: A Peruvian national was arrested by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) after authorities say she falsely claimed to be a U.S. citizen and illegally voted in the 2024 general election in Kansas, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced Thursday. Mariana Alexandra Dewey, a lawful permanent resident and citizen of Peru, was arrested by Homeland Security Investigations special agents after authorities determined she unlawfully voted in the Nov. 5, 2024, election in Sedgwick County, according to DHS. The arrest comes as the Trump administration continues its crackdown on noncitizens accused of illegally voting in U.S. elections. "This alien violated the sacred right of every American citizen," DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said in a news release. WATCH: ILLEGAL ALIEN BUSTED IN BATTLEGROUND STATE AFTER ALLEGEDLY COMMITTING VOTER FRAUD "If even one noncitizen votes, that steals the voice of a U.S. citizen," Mullin continued. "Only American citizens have the right to participate in our political and election processes, and DHS will continue to investigate, seek criminal prosecution and ultimately remove aliens who vote to ensure free, fair and honest elections." According to DHS, election records showed Dewey submitted a Kansas voter registration application and cast a provisional ballot after certifying, under penalty of perjury, that she was a U.S. citizen. NONCITIZEN CHARGED WITH VOTING IN MINNESOTA 2024 ELECTION AFTER ADMITTING ‘MISTAKE’ TO INVESTIGATORS During a subsequent interview with investigators, authorities said Dewey acknowledged she was a lawful permanent resident, not a U.S. citizen, and admitted voting in the 2024 general election. DHS said she later pleaded guilty to disorderly election conduct under Kansas law. The department said Dewey was taken into ICE custody Sept. 1 after HSI agents located her at a residence in Wichita. DHS described the arrest as the latest in the administration's effort to crack down on noncitizens accused of illegally voting in American elections. articles.title: Meet Eric Thompson, the 39-year-old Texas engineer who has collected 5,000 condiment packets, including nearly 400 Taco Bell designs and a toothpaste sachet from 1950
articles.summary: US News: Most people tear open a condiment packet, squeeze out the last drop and toss the wrapper without a second thought. Eric Thompson sees something beyond.
articles.body: Most people tear open a condiment packet, squeeze out the last drop and toss the wrapper without a second thought. Eric Thompson sees something beyond: a tiny piece of design, advertising and everyday history. Across his Texas home, thousands of these disposable packets have been transformed from fast-food leftovers into a meticulously organized archive. Meet Eric, a 39-year-old computer engineer from Helotes who has amassed roughly 5,000 single-serving sauce packets, turning an ordinary dining accessory into an unusually detailed collecting hobby.According to a report by the San Antonio Express-News, Thompson's collection spans ketchup, mustard, mayonnaise, relish, barbecue sauce, honey, jelly, seafood sauces, vinegar and numerous Asian condiments. Even Whataburger's small, box-shaped ketchup tubs have earned a place in the archive. Around 3,100 individual designs have been cataloged in his online Condiment Packet Archive, where packets are organized by brand, color, date and flavor. His collection also appears on TikTok, where he shares discoveries and the stories behind unusual designs. Hot sauce is the largest category, with about 760 designs. Taco Bell is the standout brand, accounting for nearly 400 distinct packets. The chain's wide range of sauces and frequent use of humorous packaging have made its packets particularly collectible.From a college rainbow to a serious archiveAs per the same online report, Thompson's fascination began in 2007 while he was studying at Penn State. A colorful arrangement of condiment packets caught his attention, creating what looked like a miniature rainbow across a communal food area. When the arrangement later disappeared after a vendor change, Thompson saved several of the remaining packets. What began as an appreciation for the visual arrangement gradually developed into an interest in documenting the evolution of condiment packaging. Today, he tries to collect at least three copies of each new design. One becomes part of the archive, while additional examples can be kept for trading or preservation.Cleaning, cataloging and preserving every packetThe process is considerably more involved than simply picking up discarded wrappers. Thompson carefully opens each packet, empties the contents—often using them with his meals—and then washes and dries the packaging. Once clean, the packet is cataloged and placed inside a protective plastic sleeve similar to those used for trading cards. The sleeves are organized in color-coded containers, although hundreds of packets remain in the queue awaiting processing. Thompson estimates he averages about five packets a night. The collection includes several hundred vintage examples from the 1970s, 1980s and 1990s. Its oldest item is particularly unusual: a squeezable Fuller Brush Company toothpaste packet dating to 1950.Tiny packages with a big historyThe collection also provides a window into how companies use color, typography and packaging to communicate with consumers. Red commonly signals ketchup, while yellow suggests mustard, creating visual expectations before a packet is even opened. Thompson is particularly interested in designs that break those conventions, including unusual colors and generic packaging that reveal different approaches to branding. His Heinz collection alone contains 309 different packets from the United States, Europe and the United Kingdom. Rare finds also turn up through online marketplaces and donations from collectors around the world.Preserving everyday AmericanaThompson's collection has now earned a place in Ripley's Believe It or Not! Wired into Weird, the franchise's 23rd annual collection of unusual people and discoveries. What makes the archive remarkable is not simply its size. These tiny two-by-three-inch packages document changing tastes, advertising styles, restaurant culture and consumer habits. Something designed to be used for seconds can therefore survive for decades—not because it was meant to be preserved, but because one collector recognized that even the most disposable objects can carry a story.Images Courtesy: San Antonio Express-NewsCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Peru joins US-led ‘Shield of the Americas’ security alliance
articles.summary: Fujimori administration is latest right-wing government to join alliance for a more aggressive approach against crime.
articles.body:
Peru will join the “Shield of the Americas”, a regional security alliance led by the United States that shares intelligence and cooperates in military operations against drug cartels.

Keiko Fujimori, Peru’s recently elected right-wing leader, announced the move on Thursday after talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio.

“We appreciate this opportunity [to join the initiative], because for us, having previously had to tackle terrorism, [we] know how difficult it is to confront criminality today,” Fujimori said.

Her government also awarded Rubio the Order of the Sun, one of the country’s highest civilian honours.

Rubio’s visit to the Peruvian capital, Lima, caps his three-day, three-country tour of South America to shore up ties between US President Donald Trump and conservative allies in the region.

The diplomat praised Fujimori’s decision to join the Shield of the Americas, also known as the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (ACCC), which has advocated for greater military involvement in the fight against crime.

“It is a shield against these threats to the sovereignty of these independent nations,” Rubio explained.

“It is a shield against these transnational criminal groups that, in many cases, have more money and better military equipment than the state. That is unacceptable, and the only way to defeat it is to confront it forcefully.”

Fujimori, a former first lady and the daughter of former President Alberto Fujimori, was sworn into office in July after campaigning heavily on security-related issues.

Peru is the world’s second-largest producer of cocaine, behind Colombia, and reports of crimes like extortion have spiked in recent years.

But Washington’s involvement in the region remains a controversial prospect, given its history of past interventions and its support of right-wing leaders accused of human rights abuses.

Al Jazeera correspondent Teresa Bo explained that the closer cooperation has also raised concerns about the prospect of eroding Latin American sovereignty.

“This has generated lots of fear among many people in this part of the world of what a greater influence of the United States, of what a military influence of the United States, could bring about,” she said.

Rubio attempted to tamp down those concerns during his visit, saying the US would only intervene with the permission of local authorities.

“We’re not going to do anything that our partners don’t ask us to do,” Rubio said. “We don’t want to do less than what you ask of us, but we’re not going to do more than what you ask of us.”

Nevertheless, in Lima, protesters gathered outside the government house where Fujimori’s meeting with Rubio was taking place. Some carried signs that read, “Marco Rubio out of Peru, no to Shield of the Americas.”

“We have said that Peru is nobody’s colony, and it is not the back garden of any country in the world,” Soledad Lozano, one of the protesters, said.

The Trump administration has also indicated that it would like countries like Peru distance themselves from China, which overtook the US as Peru’s primary trading partner.

In February, for instance, the Trump administration criticised Peru for allowing China to construct a mega-port in Chancay, warning that “cheap Chinese money costs sovereignty”.

“China has major investments in Peru right now,” Bo explained. “It controls a port that is 80km away from Lima, and what the US is trying to do is increase its presence in the Western Hemisphere and to try to cut a bit of economic dependency that many countries in Latin America have with China.”

Peru is critical not only to US security strategy in Latin America, but also to its economic interests. It is an important source of mineral resources, as the world’s third-largest producer of copper.

In January, Washington designated ⁠Peru a major non-NATO ally, and the US ⁠State Department approved a possible $1.5bn foreign military sale for work at Callao Naval Base, Peru’s main naval hub near Lima.

articles.title: LG defends smart-TV features amid audio surveillance allegations
articles.summary: Recent accusations against the electronics company have raised new questions about the nonconsensual data it harvests.
articles.body:
South Korean consumer-electronics company LG has denied allegations that its smart televisions record ambient conversations, listen while on standby and store recordings for later transmission.

On Wednesday, the company told Al Jazeera that voice data is only recorded when a user presses and holds the voice button on the TV remote or activates its “Hi LG” wake word, after the user has activated the Far-Field voice recognition feature.

“Other than these instances, the TVs do not collect or record ambient conversations,” LG said, adding that voice data is only processed via explicit user commands.

“The audio is immediately deleted if the wake word is not recognised,” the company said.

The statement comes after a 135-minute investigative report released on Monday by a popular tech media outlet and YouTube channel, Gamers Nexus, with Level1Techs and independent security researchers. The investigation examined LG televisions’ data collection and security systems, raising questions about how the devices handle users’ private information.

By analysing network traffic and software, the researchers purport to have discovered that these televisions actively track users and harvest a glut of local network data, including audio transcripts.

Inside LG’s controversial tracking system

Gamers Nexus said its researchers were able to record audio through an LG television while it was in a state of hibernation, meaning that even if the microphone switch on the TV is turned off, other microphones exposed to the TV might not be, such as the remote.

The result, Gamers Nexus says, is “216,000,000 Spy TVs” in the US alone.

On its website, LG says it has 49 million smarts TVs in the US and 216 million globally.

Recorded background noise in the room, including as far as 12 metres (40 feet) away from the TV, was also being archived, they said.

Yash Vekaria, a computer science researcher at the University of California, Davis, says that because TVs stay in homes for years, often past their update support, “prompt patching from LG matters”.

“This vulnerability can allow sniffing [of] much more critical conversations … Imagine government officials discussing national security in their hotel room [next to an] LG TV”, Vekaria said.

The researchers further alleged that unmatched wake-word interactions or unclear sounds could remain stored locally, transcribed and preserved on the device as plain text in case the local network is disconnected and uploaded later to LG servers.

Copies can stay in temporary storage spaces, known as buffers, without the user knowing, Vekaria said.

Privacy risks generally stem from poor design and selective disclosure. The more disconcerting threat lies in a compromised device, Vekaria added, which could be made to execute any command its hardware allows.

The researchers also said they found text transcripts derived from audio captured by the television, even after 10-15 seconds of silence after invoking “Hi LG”.

The claims have not been independently verified by Al Jazeera.

“It raises a question of purpose,” says Vekaria, “a voice command is only useful in real time, so audio queued for later upload is presumably being kept for something else, such as logging, analytics or model training. LG should explain what”.

Vekaria says he is not aware of any concrete evidence that ambient audio or transcripts feed into LG’s advertising or profiling systems.

“What we do know is that LG runs an advertising business built on household data, including the Automatic Content Recognition [ACR] tracking documented in our research , and that its voice pipeline appears to capture and retain more than users would expect.”

Still, there may be simpler explanations, he says, “such as diagnostics or improving speech recognition … but even those involve keeping recordings from people’s homes without meaningful consent”.

The researchers also said that the televisions scanned home networks for other devices and collected information including internal IP addresses, nearby Wi-Fi networks and location data.

LG said scanning for nearby devices is a “standard” smart-TV function.

Device discovery can serve “legitimate functions” such as screen casting, media sharing and connecting smart-home products, like Amazon’s Alexa, said Anna Maria Mandalari, a lecturer in communications and networking at University College London.

LG stated that ACR, voice recognition and interest-based advertising are all “separate features”, each requiring “explicit user opt-in consent” and each of which can be disabled through the TV’s settings.

Depending on how device discovery is implemented, Mandalari said, a television may “obtain the names, addresses, manufacturers and types of other devices on a household network” – information that can reveal the composition of a home and help “create a broader profile of its occupants”.

LG’s advertising arm, LG Ad Solutions, has openly marketed the breadth of information it can derive from connected households. Corporate videos featured in the Gamers Nexus investigation show LG representatives saying: “We know who is in the LG household,” and, “We know which devices are there.”

LG told Al Jazeera that it was “committed to providing transparency” and that it rejected “deceptive practices”.
